summary: Review of evidence through January 29, 2024 shows no inadequacies in the existing covenant package; all clauses are retained and no new protections are warranted, resulting in no material drift.

clauses.rationale: Evidence of a $94M Amazon termination fee with $35M immediate repayment triggers existing step-down mechanics but reveals no flaw in the Minimum Core Assets Test clause.
No evidence indicates a need to change financial statement delivery, going-concern exceptions, or budget requirements; current reporting remains appropriate.
No evidence suggests monthly deliverables or compliance certification need adjustment; existing frequency and content remain fit.
Evidence confirms the Amazon Break Fee will be paid and applied as described; the sweep provisions already cover this scenario, so no change needed.
No evidence of developments affecting notice-of-default procedures; the existing notice requirement remains sufficient.

drift_reasons: No dated evidence justifies tightening, loosening, or adding protections; the current package already accommodates the Amazon Break Fee payment and related terms.
